outcome: birth mode (planned cesarean, emergency cesarean, vaginal birth rate)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 16,110 live, singleton pregnancies whose medical records were reviewed from June 2018 to February 2022.
finding: Caseload midwifery care was associated with fewer planned and emergency cesareans, less postpartum hemorrhage, and fewer low Apgar scores, while also leading to more amniotomies and early discharges.
mod_finding: Caseload midwifery was associated with a higher vaginal birth rate, primarily due to a lower likelihood of planned and emergency cesareans.
